key_insight: A temporal machine learning, time-to-event model can personalize predictions of ALS functional decline and wheelchair use by combining longitudinal ALSFRS-R trajectories with survival analysis.
clinical_relevance: This could help clinicians anticipate milestone timing, support proactive care planning, and improve trial stratification for people living with ALS.
method: Integrated longitudinal ALSFRS-R, activities of daily living, diagnosis, and demographic data into a harmonized cohort.
Used correlation-based clustering plus generalized additive mixed models to map nonlinear decline across functional domains.
Built a temporal machine learning time-to-event framework with Cox modeling to generate individualized wheelchair-free survival curves.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a harmonized longitudinal dataset and stage-dependent modeling that identified lower limb function, especially walking and stair climbing, as the strongest predictor of earlier wheelchair access.
watch_item: Because the model is data-driven and cohort-specific, external validation and careful handling of missing or irregular follow-up would be important before routine deployment.
paper_title: A Temporal Machine Learning-Based Time-to-Event Model for Predicting ALS Progression and Healthcare Utilization
